target_customer: Electronics and hardware engineers who need PCB symbols, footprints and 3D models; component suppliers who pay to distribute models; later users of an AI design copilot
problem: Engineers spend hours creating digital models of components from scratch before they can lay out a circuit board.
business_model: Free to engineers; revenue from component suppliers and distributors that sponsor or distribute models, plus the AI design tool
product_category: Electronic design automation component library and AI copilot

founders.name: Natasha Baker
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2023-10-10) calls her an electrical engineer frustrated by slow circuit board processes. Education and employers not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: The 2015 product was a searchable library of symbols, footprints and 3D models, built largely by aggregating and generating CAD data. The hard part was data quality at scale, not research-grade technology. The 2023 AI copilot is harder but is not the founding product.

defensibility.rationale: A large verified model library and supplier partnerships (TE Connectivity, Samtec, Texas Instruments per TechCrunch) are slow to replicate, but models can be rebuilt and incumbents also offer libraries.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: These vendors still compete as of 2026 comparison pages. Octopart's marketplace aggregates models from partners including SnapEDA. No acquisition of SnapEDA was found.

market_need_then: Engineers repeatedly rebuild component models by hand; the founder cites this pain in TechCrunch. SnapEDA launched in 2013 and joined YC Summer 2015 per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: snapeda.com used until the 2023 rebrand to snapmagic.com; purchase details not found.

identity.logo: EE Journal headline contrasts a sad face logo with a happy face logo after the rebrand; design not otherwise described
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, engineer-to-engineer; the company describes itself as built by electrical engineers for electrical engineers.

rebrands.why: Rebrand launched with the AI copilot; coverage frames it as extending the company beyond a CAD library, but no source states why the name Magic was chosen.

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press covered the rebrand (EE Journal, eeNews Europe, TechCrunch). No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Used by over 1.5 million engineers per TechCrunch and carried by major distributors, with trade coverage of the rebrand. No evidence the name itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Free CAD model library for engineers
pivots.to: AI copilot for circuit board design under the SnapMagic name
pivots.why: Founder says the proprietary model database positions the company to bring AI to hardware engineers (TechCrunch 2023-10-10).

outcome_analysis: SnapEDA built a free library of electronic component models that reached over 1.5 million engineers and partnered with suppliers such as TE Connectivity and Samtec, which gave it distribution that rivals had to buy. Funding found is small and mostly unverified until an undisclosed round led by Bow Capital in October 2023, when it rebranded to SnapMagic and added an AI design copilot. It is still independent and active, but its outcome is not yet clear.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights says 120K dollars seed from Y Combinator dated 2016-03-24 and Seedtable dates a seed to 2023-10 with no amount; the 2023 round is recorded as other because TechCrunch gives no stage or amount. Competitors: no source dated 2015 was found; 2026 comparison pages name Ultra Librarian, SamacSys and Octopart, which is not competition as of founding, so the list is empty. Natasha Baker is the only founder named by the YC page and TechCrunch.
